fleetMemory.LESSON: A join miss and a verified absence can hide behind the same string. The signal that distinguishes them must be read from the layer that emits it (here isCadJoinMissBasis), never reconstructed from the state it produced -- if you test for 'absent-verified' you cannot tell a fabricated absence from a real one, and the sweep that removes the first also destroys the second.

Two-namespace counties fail in BOTH directions, and the direction depends on which population you are standing on: the publish compared served keys against an index that cannot hold them (P-319), while the writer is served keys whose roll rows carry no values (P-310). Same county, same split, opposite symptoms -- so every claim about a keyspace must name the population it was measured on.

The cheaper-looking recovery is often already in the store. WCAD publishes its own R<->numeric pair in one row of a dataset this repo has been ingesting for months; the address-based recovery the bake uses is the expensive, error-prone approximation of an identifier that was sitting in a staging table.
fleetMemory.DEAD-END: Renewing a heavy-scan lease after expiry: refused, and the refusal is trivially lost in a pipeline. Renew before expiry. Also: inline `node -e` SQL through PowerShell -Command mangles count(*); write the query to a file.
